question: A 22-year-old man comes to the physician because of generalized fatigue for the past 3 months. During this time, his grades have declined in his college courses because he has had difficulty focusing on assignments and sometimes sleeps in class. He no longer plays the drums for his band and has stopped attending family events. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 60/min, and blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. On mental status examination, he describes his mood as “ok.” He has a flat affect. There is no evidence of suicidal ideation. His speech is slow in rate and monotone in rhythm, and his thought process is organized. He has no delusions or hallucinations. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in treatment?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Possible major depressive disorder -> Symptoms of fatigue, difficulty focusing, social withdrawal -> Low mood and flat affect -> Slow speech and monotone rhythm -> Organized thought process -> No delusions or hallucinations -> Consideration of antidepressant therapy -> 70%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms of fatigue, difficulty focusing, social withdrawal, flat affect, slow speech, and monotone rhythm, suggestive of major depressive disorder. Given the absence of suicidal ideation and organized thought process, initial treatment should involve psychotherapy and/or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) like escitalopram. Close monitoring for any worsening symptoms or emergence of suicidal thoughts is essential.
